questions.knowledge_point: Integrating Functions Containing the Natural Logarithm
questions.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{4x}\cdot 4\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}=\frac{3}{x}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{6\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})}{x}\,\text{d}x & =6\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x}\cdot  \\  & =6\int u\cdot (\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{6}{3}\int u\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & ={u}^{2}+C \\  & ={ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})+C\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$

$$

questions.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{5}⁡(3x).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{x{log}_{5}⁡(3x)}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{{log}_{5}⁡(3x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡5\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡5\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡5\operatorname{ln}⁡|{log}_{5}⁡(3x)|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{7}⁡(4x).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡7}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡7\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x{log}_{7}⁡(4x)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{log}_{7}⁡(4x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡7\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡7\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡7\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡7\operatorname{ln}⁡|{log}_{7}⁡(4x)|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}).$Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,⟹\,\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int u\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\,\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\int u\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3{log}_{3}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{5}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3}{x{log}_{5}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{{log}_{5}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡5\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡5\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡5\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡5\operatorname{ln}⁡|{log}_{5}⁡x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{6}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡6}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡6\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{log}_{6}^{2}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =3\int ({log}_{6}⁡x)^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =3\int {u}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡6\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡6\int {u}^{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡6\cdot \frac{{u}^{3}}{3}+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡6\cdot {log}_{6}^{3}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{4}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $4$ | $16$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{16}\frac{2}{x{log}_{4}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{1}{{log}_{4}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =2{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{2})\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\  & =4{ln}^{2}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | ${e}^{2}$ | ${e}^{3}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $3$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{3}}\frac{1}{5x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{3}}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2x}\cdot 2\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e/2$ | $1/2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $0$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}\frac{1}{x\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1/2}^{e/2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\frac{{u}^{1/2}}{1/2}|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2\cdot {\sqrt{u}|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2(\sqrt{1}-\sqrt{0}) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{7}⁡(\frac{x}{3}).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡7}\cdot \frac{1}{3}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡7}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡7\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $3$ | $21$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{21}\frac{1}{x}{log}_{7}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{3}^{21}{log}_{7}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡7\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡7{\int }_{0}^{1}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡7\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{2}\cdot (1-0) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x).$ Then  we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{4x}\cdot 4=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $e$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡4$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡4e$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)}{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{1}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4e}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot {\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4e} \\  & ={\frac{3}{4}\cdot {u}^{2}|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4e} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}((\operatorname{ln}⁡4e)^{2}-(\operatorname{ln}⁡4)^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Integrating Functions Containing the Natural Logarithm
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's set $u = \ln x.$ Then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= \dfrac 1 x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}u=\dfrac 1 x\,{\textrm{d}x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3}{x\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\int {u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\cdot 2{u}^{1/2}+C \\  & =6\sqrt{u}+C \\  & =6\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the integral $\displaystyle \int \dfrac{\log^2_3 x }{x} \,\textrm d x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as

$$
\int \dfrac{(\log_3 x)^2 }{x} \,\textrm d x.
$$

Let $u=\log_3 x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = \dfrac{1}{x\ln 3}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\ln 3\,\textrm d u = \dfrac 1 x \textrm d x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int ({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {u}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\int {u}^{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \frac{1}{3}{u}^{3}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3({log}_{3}⁡x)^{3}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3{log}_{3}^{3}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u = \ln x.$ Then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= \dfrac 1 x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}u=\dfrac 1 x\,{\textrm{d}x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e$ | $e^2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\eqalign{
	\int_{e}^{e^2} \dfrac{\ln^2 x}{x}\,\textrm{d}x
&= \int_{e}^{e^2} (\ln x)^2\cdot \dfrac{\textrm{d}x}{x}\[5pt]
&=\int_{1}^{2} u^2\,\textrm{d}u\[5pt]
&=\left.\dfrac13u^{3}\right|_{1}^{2}\[5pt] 
&=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(2^3-1^3 \right)\[5pt]
&=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(8-1 \right)\[5pt]
&=\dfrac{7}{3}		

	}
$$
